text:
Tampa Bay hosts Seattle tonight, and the model sees the home side as the better team, projecting 3.39 expected goals for TBL against 2.69 for SEA. The Lightning generate 3.47 expected goals per 60 and allow 2.70, while the Kraken sit at 3.15 for and 3.31 against. Seattle has scored four goals a game and allowed 2.71, but its chance quality (47 percent of expected goals at 5-on-5) suggests the results are running ahead of the play. Tampa Bay sits at 56 percent, and its power play (0.68 expected goals a game) and penalty kill (0.58 allowed) both edge Seattle's 0.60 and 0.54, though the Kraken's kill is slightly tighter. Both teams played last night's equivalent on one day of rest.

In goal, projected starter Andrei Vasilevskiy has a .890 save percentage and roughly break-even goals saved above expected (-0.05) through five games, but last season he was 23.15 goals better than expected over 58 appearances. Projected Seattle starter Joey Daccord is at .910 and +1.11 this year after a -6.10 mark across 47 games last season. Form points the same direction for both: Tampa Bay controlled the chances in four of its last five before a 4-1 loss at the Rangers, while Seattle won three straight on the road, the last in a shootout at Philadelphia, despite being outchanced in most of them.

The model likes Brandon Hagel to score at 45 percent, with Nikita Kucherov (35 percent) and Jake Guentzel (34 percent) behind him. Kucherov is also given a 44 percent chance at two or more points. For Seattle, Bobby McMann leads at 26 percent to score, with Jared McCann and Jordan Eberle both at 25.
